newsitem.title: FRANCE: De Silguy says two-country EMU legal but unlikely.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy says two-country EMU legal but unlikely.

text.p: Launching a single European currency with just two founder countries would be legally possible but practically unlikely, European Economic Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Tuesday.
"From a legal point of view, economic and monetary union (EMU) could operate with only two member states," the French Commissioner said in reply to Euro-MPs' questions.

"The European Commission feels that without France and without Germany or without a significant number of other member states, the advantages of EMU would be significantly diminished," de Silguy said.

"The Commission is convinced that a significant number of countries will be able to participate in EMU from the outset," he said, adding that EU countries would decide "as early as possible in 1998" on when to go ahead with the planned currency union.
